subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth refresh succeeds but cron/heartbeat fail with 10s auth refresh timeout

question: Should OpenClaw mitigate the Codex app-server's 10-second external-auth callback deadline by returning cached usable ChatGPT tokens instead of force-refreshing every callback, or should this remain blocked on upstream Codex configurability and broader auth-deadline work?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the durable fix changes auth freshness, provider recovery, and possibly security expectations for when a Codex app-server refresh request may reuse cached credentials.

options.title: Adopt an OpenClaw bridge mitigation
options.body: Prefer returning a still-usable cached token or another bounded OpenClaw-side response for refresh callbacks, with regression coverage proving valid auth no longer trips the upstream 10-second deadline.

options.title: Wait for upstream timeout configurability
options.body: Keep this issue open but do not change OpenClaw behavior until the Codex app-server exposes a longer or configurable external-auth timeout.

options.title: Scope this issue to diagnostics only
options.body: Accept the existing refresh behavior and limit OpenClaw work to clearer reauth/status guidance plus linked auth-deadline/failover issues.

recommendation.title: Adopt an OpenClaw bridge mitigation
recommendation.body: Prefer returning a still-usable cached token or another bounded OpenClaw-side response for refresh callbacks, with regression coverage proving valid auth no longer trips the upstream 10-second deadline.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest routing signal is recent Codex app-server/auth bridge ownership in the exact files and prior maintainer-facing Codex OAuth bridge work.
